messages.subject: hBayesDM in food chain
messages.body_plain: My focus is on utilizing Hierarchical Bayesian Analysis (HBA) to analyze the bioaccumulation process of  organic contaminants in the  food chain, as well as how environmental factors impact this process.  I require the construction of a hierarchical Bayesian model using the hBayesDM package in R, aimed at quantifying the influence of temperature on the enrichment of antibiotics in the planktonic planktonic food web and on the efficiency of food chain transfer. I am learning from here https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-021-03352-2. Where can I start this modeling process？

messages.subject: Hierarchical Gaussian Filter (HGFs)
messages.body_plain:
Dear hBayesDM developers, Dear all users,

I would like to fit a Hierarchical Gaussian Filter (HGF) to my data.

I noticed that there is no HGF in the lastest version of hBayesDM. However, I indeed found the Stan scripts for HGF on one github branch of our hBayesDM.

https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/tree/feature/add-hgf-models/commons/stan_files

I am confused, may I know are these HGFs have been tested and validated? Or the HGFs is still under developing?

Best,
Ted
Post-doc at the University College London, UK.
Computational Neuroscience

messages.subject: Re: hBayesDM in food chain
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

If you are looking for which model to start from, referring to the list <https://ccs-lab.github.io/hBayesDM/reference/index.html> of models in hBayesDM could be helpful. In case you are interested in some classic books to start with, Kruschke's puppy book (for Bayesian analysis), Farell & Lewandowsky (general modeling), or Lee & Wagenmakers (2013)'s are my recommendations. We would be happy to discuss more about your next steps.

Best,
JH

Jeung-Hyun Lee
PhD candidate,
Computational Clinical Science Lab.
Department of Psychology
Seoul National University
Building 16, Room A107
Email : jhlee...@snu.ac.kr
Website : https://jeunghyunlee.github.io/
